note:
FOLLOW-UP / PRODUCTION-INTEGRATION GAP discovered during review of today's closed SceneIssues. The completed `20260828-210700-000-WorldbuildingGalleryTownArchitectureShowcase` correctly followed its written scope by building six town-style programs and demonstrating them in `WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase`. However, the intended product result is that the Kentridge town architecture is actually used in the real `KentridgePlayableSlice`, not left as gallery-only showcase content. The gallery may remain as a development/reference showcase, but it is not a substitute for production integration.

SCOPE: Integrate the reusable Kentridge WorldBuilder town-architecture program and detail vocabulary created by the gallery feature into the actual Kentridge town in `Assets/Scenes/KentridgePlayableSlice.unity`. Do NOT place Hightown, Moordell, Rossdam, Fairy Village, or Orc Village physically inside Kentridge; those styles remain reusable for their eventual production towns. This ticket is specifically about making the real Kentridge playable town use the Kentridge architecture system.

PRODUCTION EXPECTATION: The playable Kentridge settlement should visibly inherit the reference-driven pastoral Kentridge language already authored: warm fieldstone foundations/well, cream/tan plaster, exposed timber framing, weathered wood, appropriate roofs, grounded porches/steps/fences/paths, and reusable 10-30 cm construction detail. The actual town should include recognizable production roles such as cottages/residences, inn/pub, church/civic building, shops, warehouse/storehouse, and the Kentridge well/landmark where those roles exist in the playable slice. Reuse the shared architecture APIs and production town program; do not copy gallery geometry or hand-author a second Kentridge-only implementation.

COMPATIBILITY: Preserve current Kentridge gameplay/story/traversal systems and semantic anchors. Existing opening/cutscene, NPC, combat, road, vegetation, landmark, and building-role integrations must continue to resolve after the architecture replacement/integration. If current gameplay depends on old footprint/opening anchors, adapt the production composition through semantic WorldBuilder contracts rather than hard-coded scene coordinates.

VISUAL CLOSURE BAR: Inspect the exact built `KentridgePlayableSlice` directly. Gallery screenshots do not count. Durable evidence must show normal gameplay traversal through the real Kentridge town, including wide/player-height/close views of representative Kentridge buildings and the well/other recognizable landmark context. The architecture must visibly demonstrate the shared meso/micro detail vocabulary at gameplay distance and close range, with believable entrances, windows, roof transitions, supports, circulation, grounding, and no unintended intersections. Compare the result against the Kentridge Mounting Force reference screenshot family and the repository AAA world-authoring bar.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) `KentridgePlayableSlice` composes the shared Kentridge WorldBuilder town-architecture program for its production town rather than relying on gallery-only content; (2) representative Kentridge production buildings visibly use the intended material, silhouette, roof/form, opening, timber/masonry, and 10-30 cm detail vocabulary; (3) the real Kentridge well/landmark language is present and recognizable where applicable; (4) player circulation and building entrances remain usable and existing story/gameplay semantic anchors continue to work; (5) no direct scene voxel-writing, copied gallery geometry, or Kentridge-only duplicate architecture backend is introduced; (6) focused behavioral regressions prove the production playable-slice composition resolves through the shared Kentridge program and preserves key gameplay/anchor contracts; (7) the exact built-application Kentridge harness reaches a usable rendered scene and physically traverses/inspects the integrated town without startup/runtime exceptions; (8) durable built-player visual evidence, not semantic counts alone, proves the production result meets the reference/AAA bar; and (9) blast radius, build/world-generation cost, memory, draw/triangle/streaming implications, and likely regressions to existing Kentridge systems are checked before closure.
